sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling from a full-data law with consistency and conditional exchangeability.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent units with \(X\in\mathbb T^d\), binary treatment, and outcomes in the standard Borel space \(\mathcal Y\); two-outcome laws are used only as least-favorable submodels.
sampling_model.treatment: Unknown Hölder propensity \(e\) with fixed overlap; a comparison experiment supplies \(e\) to the test.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitted propensity and arm-law estimation, followed by a block-local empirical higher-order correction and, for Wald statistics, a cross-fitted covariance estimate.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper gives a test with valid type 1 error and consistency against fixed alternatives.
The minimax lower bound is attained by a local polynomial R-Learner under additional design-density conditions.

Version 5 proves semiparametric efficiency without covariate-density smoothness for the scalar mean under missing at random, and extends the construction to a class of scalar doubly robust functionals, using an empirical Gram basis with \(k=o(n)\).
Spectral regularization is minimax optimal with a smaller separation boundary than MMD in direct two-sample testing.
A moderated kernel test attains source-class goodness-of-fit rates that ordinary MMD can miss.
MMDAgg is minimax adaptive over Sobolev balls up to an iterated logarithmic term.
Cross-fitted one-step estimators can be efficient for differentiable Hilbert-valued parameters.
A characteristic outcome kernel makes the unsmoothed pointwise conditional discrepancy identify equality of conditional laws.
Random design changes the minimax rate for nonparametric variance estimation.
Occupancy-aware binning attains minimax conditional-independence testing rates under smooth conditional laws.

body.tldr: The flagship question is whether the all-tests SCoDiTE separation radius under an arbitrary covariate density bounded above and below equals the explicit candidate \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\), which balances Hölder bias against a pair-occupancy and empirical-Gram inflation functional built from primitive cell probabilities. The converse is anchored by full \(2\times2\) Bernoulli cell tables: the null law factorizes and has \(U=0\), while the alternative does not factorize and has \(U_\omega=2u_\omega v_\omega b_Y/(1-u_\omega^2)\neq0\). Shared signs and disjoint bump supports make the one-record mixtures identical, while explicit Hölder, overlap, covariance-sandwich, source-norm, signal, and \(n\)-mixture bounds yield the slower uniform-design radius \(n^{-2(\beta_e+\beta_m)/(2(\beta_e+\beta_m)+d)}\) for \(0<s\le1/2\) below the smoothness elbow. Under its stated nondegeneracy condition, the known-propensity experiment has a root-\(n\) RKHS-norm boundary. Above the elbow, the declared assumptions deliver a density-robust root-\(n\) upper bound; the matching lower bound requires only the separately stated regular constant-contrast path. Once the arbitrary-density modulus is settled, an eigenwise iff criterion compares higher-order SKCD--MMD with regularized SKCD--Wald, and a jointly calibrated grid selects regularization and correction rank. Characteristicness of the outcome kernel does not by itself convert the covariate-smoothed moment null into pointwise conditional homogeneity.

project_justification.gap: Existing SCoDiTE theory is first order and pointwise in the law, direct spectral tests omit causal nuisances, and the empirical-HOIF theorem of Liu et al. treats scalar missing-at-random and doubly robust functionals with \(k=o(n)\). It therefore does not settle rough SCoDiTE scales with \(K_h>n\), although that non-subsumption alone is not evidence that occupancy worsens the rate.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied flagship object is the all-tests separation modulus for a Hilbert-valued causal moment under only a positive bounded design density, expressed through a falsifiable primitive occupancy--Gram candidate and matched by legal exact-null causal experiments.
project_justification.fill: The candidate \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\) records cell-pair availability and empirical-Gram inflation. The displayed \(P_\omega,Q_\omega\) tables separate a factorizing exact-null law from a nonfactorizing alternative with \(U_\omega=2u_\omega v_\omega b_Y/(1-u_\omega^2)\), and the legality lemma derives positivity, overlap, both Hölder memberships, nonzero \(\Psi\), covariance stability, the \(0<s\le1/2\) source bound, and mixture affinity from the construction. A collision-based higher-order score supplies the arbitrary-density attainment handle, and the resulting modulus feeds the spectral iff and adaptive-grid questions. In the high-smoothness branch the score yields the root-\(n\) upper bound under the declared assumptions, while equality uses a separately stated nondegenerate constant-contrast path only for the local lower-bound reduction.

body.related_work: Jain and Luedtke (2026) define the SCoDiTE moment, its efficient Hilbert influence function, and fixed-operator MMD and Wald tests; their product-rate theorem and fixed-alternative consistency supply the starting experiment. Their local asymptotic theory also motivates the ordinary root-\(n\) lower-bound reduction, which here is invoked only under an explicit nondegenerate quadratic-mean differentiable constant-contrast path inside the declared class. Park, Shalit, Schölkopf, and Muandet (2021) study an unsmoothed pointwise conditional embedding discrepancy; that result motivates comparison but does not justify the maintained Hilbert-valued periodic Hölder condition and does not identify the quotient null after covariate smoothing. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) supply the localized fuzzy-hypothesis architecture, but the present paired construction requires a different nonfactorizing alternative cell table so that the null has \(U=0\) and the alternative has the explicit nonzero Hilbert contrast. Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins (2026, arXiv:1705.07577v5) prove semiparametric efficiency without density smoothness for a scalar missing-at-random mean and a class of scalar doubly robust functionals using empirical Gram bases with \(k=o(n)\); this informs the upper-bound handle but does not cover Hilbert testing or \(K_h>n\). Hagrass, Sriperumbudur, and Li (2024) and Balasubramanian, Li, and Yuan (2021) supply direct-sample spectral extremal arguments under a different separation metric. Schrab et al. (2023) supply the dependent-grid calibration template. Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han (2020) and Neykov, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman (2021) show in adjacent random-design problems that occupancy can enter minimax rates and test construction. None of these papers states the candidate occupancy--Gram SCoDiTE frontier or jointly supplies the exact-null cell algebra, covariance sandwich, source bound, and mixture-affinity calculation used here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: For the early kill case \(d=1\), \(\beta_e=\beta_m=0.2\), the uniform-design benchmark is \(n^{-4/9}\) and its nominal partition size is \(K_h\asymp n^{10/9}>n\). This lies outside Liu et al.'s proved \(k=o(n)\) empirical-HOIF regime and establishes non-subsumption only. The corrected fuzzy construction settles the componentwise cell algebra: \(p_\omega\) factorizes, \(q_\omega\) does not, and their shared-sign one-record mixtures agree. The remaining early-kill audit is the upper procedure over the full density band and the match between its empirical-Gram fluctuation and \(\Gamma_n(h;P_X)\); failure requires replacing the candidate primitive functional. The rough lower theorem also requires interior Hölder radii and a fixed kernel whose Fourier profile yields the declared covariance constants, while the model in general permits kernels without a constant Fourier mode. The two-outcome family is a proof device inside the general outcome-law model; an attaining procedure must still handle the multivariate wealth outcome in the 401(k) illustration.
body.honest_scope: The known-propensity root-\(n\) benchmark, the corrected rough uniform-design lower branch, the high-smoothness empirical-HOIF upper branch, and the Fourier quotient-null theorem are posed for proof. The rough lower branch explicitly derives the exact null, nonzero alternative, overlap, propensity and arm-embedding Hölder bounds, covariance eigen-profile stability, the \(0<s\le1/2\) source norm, and bounded mixture affinity; it is conditional only on positive radius slack and a fixed kernel with the stated Fourier profile, not on assumed fuzzy-family membership. In the high-smoothness branch, the matching root-\(n\) lower bound and thus the two-sided minimax equality are conditional on the explicitly stated class-richness premise. The flagship answer-open content is the rough arbitrary-density equivalence with the candidate occupancy--Gram radius; the candidate may be refuted and replaced by a matched primitive functional. The spectral iff classification and adaptive grid calibration remain downstream open questions. No claim is made that \(K_h>n\) itself proves an occupancy penalty, or that characteristic constituent kernels automatically make the smoothed null identical to conditional homogeneity. Under \(e\equiv1/2\), uniform \(P_X\), and a nonzero constant low-frequency contrast, the construction reduces to bounded Hilbert-mean testing with root-\(n\) separation.
